summary: Reviewed cold clone at 69c8bad4 (branch ci/yoga-gpu-lock) against PMAT-4469's three acceptance criteria. Ran: actionlint on .github/workflows/cuda-nightly.yml (clean, no output). Extracted both new 'Host GPU lock' shell steps via yq and ran bash -n on each (syntax OK). Reproduced flock semantics in a scratch dir: held a lock with `setsid flock LOCK sleep 5` in the background, then ran `flock -E 175 -w 1 LOCK true` against the held lock foreground and got exit 175, matching the '-E 175 = not free' claim and the -w 600 (=10min) comment math. Verified the case-pattern self-check (`"flock "*" $l") ;;`) actually matches the literal env var value via a standalone bash -c test (MATCH). Confirmed job names: cuda-nightly.yml job is 'ada-yoga' (matches ticket AC1/AC3), ci/sections.yml job is 'cuda-unit' (matches AC1). Confirmed the two host-lock-presence checks differ correctly per environment: ada-yoga (bare host runner) checks the file is root-owned; cuda-unit (containerized) checks /run/lock/fleet-gpu is a mountpoint before checking file presence — matching AC2's 'bind mount in the container; root-owned file on the host runner' distinction, cited directly from the diff. CARGO_TARGET_X86_64_UNKNOWN_LINUX_GNU_RUNNER is the correct Cargo env-var form (CARGO_TARGET_<UPPER_SNAKE_TRIPLE>_RUNNER) and only wraps produced-binary execution (test/bench/run), not rustc compilation, consistent with the 'compiling holds no lock' comment (asserted from general Cargo knowledge, not executed here since no cargo build was run per instructions). Checked git history: no prior GPU lock existed on either job in origin/main (git show origin/main:.github/workflows/cuda-nightly.yml showed no lock env/step at those lines), so this is a pure addition, not a weakening. docs/roadmaps/entries/PMAT-4469.yaml and the tail of docs/roadmaps/roadmap.yaml are byte-identical (diff), and the new roadmap.yaml entry is appended after the prior last entry (PMAT-4421-family, unrelated topic) at EOF, which is normal placement for a topic with no existing family in the roadmap (grep found no pre-existing gpu-lock/fleet-gpu entries to append after). AC3 ('the yoga cuda-unit job is green on a runner that has the mount') is not independently verifiable from a cold clone/no-CI-run review and the ticket itself is InProgress/50% — not treated as a blocker since the brief instructs judging the diff against the ticket text, not requiring a live CI receipt that doesn't exist yet. No test asserts the opposite of the ticket, no gate was weakened, and the diff does nothing outside the ticket's scope (only touches the two named jobs plus roadmap/ticket bookkeeping).
